Calculate Spearman rank correlations

Source: R/spearman.R
spearman.Rd

Calculate Spearman rank correlations, like Stata's spearman, stats(rho obs p). By default, as in Stata, rows missing any selected variable are excluded from every correlation (casewise deletion). Use .pairwise = TRUE for Stata's pw option.

Usage

spearman(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .pairwise = FALSE,
  .wide = FALSE,
  .adjust = c("none", "bonferroni", "sidak")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<tidy-select> or <data-masking> Columns to select or compute with select_or_transmute(). Existing columns, selection helpers, and named expressions can be mixed. Results must be numeric or logical vector columns. Matrix columns are unsupported. Omit to use every numeric or logical vector column; other columns are then skipped. Selecting another type is an error.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping variables. Grouped data use their groups unless .by is supplied. Select existing columns only; create new grouping columns with dplyr::mutate() first.

.pairwise

If TRUE, each pair uses every row where both variables are observed, like Stata's spearman, pw. The default FALSE uses one common complete sample.

.wide

If TRUE, return the correlation matrix as Stata prints it: one row per variable and the lower triangle filled, without n or p.

.adjust

"none" (default), "bonferroni" or "sidak", like Stata's bonferroni and sidak options. Adjust p-values separately within each group; not available with .wide = TRUE.

Value

An ungrouped tibble with:

  • By default, one row per distinct variable pair and group, with any grouping keys, var1, var2, r (Spearman's rho), n (observations), and p (two-sided p-value).

  • With .wide = TRUE, one row per variable and group, with grouping keys, variable, and one correlation column per variable. The diagonal is 1 and the upper triangle is NA; n and p are omitted.

Undefined correlations and p-values are NA. With fewer than three observations, p is NA even when the correlation is defined.

Details

Ties receive average ranks, and ranks are computed within each sample used for a correlation. The p-value tests independence as Stata 18 and later do: a beta distribution is fitted to the first four exact permutation moments of the statistic, with a normal approximation, sqrt(n - 1) * r, when n = 3 or no valid fit exists. Earlier Stata versions and stats::cor.test() use other approximations, so their p-values can differ. Columns are selected, computed and grouped as in pwcorr(). Like Stata's spearman, weights are not supported. A constant variable gives NA, where Stata reports a correlation of 1.

spearman() is the same as pwcorr(.method = "spearman", .listwise = TRUE); with .pairwise = TRUE it is the same as pwcorr(.method = "spearman").

References

Stata spearman manual.

See also

pwcorr(), corr(), stats::cor()

Other tabulation functions: corr(), pwcorr(), tab()

Examples

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.864    53 5.61e-14
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.799    53 2.48e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 2.20e-11

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater, .pairwise = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.861    67 3.37e-17
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.800    54 1.44e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 2.20e-11

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, .by = region)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   region               var1  var2      r     n        p
#>   <dbl+lbl>            <chr> <chr> <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] lexp  gnppc 0.880    43 4.06e-12
#> 2 2 [North America]    lexp  gnppc 0.878    14 1.63e- 4
#> 3 3 [South America]    lexp  gnppc 0.740    10 1.72e- 2

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater, .adjust = "bonferroni")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   var1  var2          r     n        p
#>   <chr> <chr>     <dbl> <int>    <dbl>
#> 1 lexp  gnppc     0.864    53 1.68e-13
#> 2 lexp  safewater 0.799    53 7.44e-11
#> 3 gnppc safewater 0.800    53 6.59e-11

spearman(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc, safewater, .wide = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   variable   lexp  gnppc safewater
#>   <chr>     <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 lexp      1     NA            NA
#> 2 gnppc     0.864  1            NA
#> 3 safewater 0.799  0.800         1
